Needs changes before merge. This is a safety-tier review because the PR changes posted G-code.

The trial merge with upstream main `f85163b0ca948250fd6a51360d14754a282e0340` was clean. I read the current upstream `AGENTS.md`.

What looks good:

- The new modules state their provenance. The jet law has separate state from the torch law.
- The new NC goldens show the water and abrasive order. I checked every new golden line. No existing golden moved.
- The diff has no UI, dependency, workflow, script-directory, or build-script change.

Local results:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: PASS. All 1,007 steps passed in 43.9 minutes. The CL change selects the batch plan.
- The gate built all selected crates locally with `--no-run`. All selected default suites passed.
- `cargo clippy -j 16 -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: PASS.
- `waterjet_engine`: 12 passed. The CL library: 49 passed, including the three new jet tests.
- The UI library: 1,337 passed and 7 ignored. Pixel snapshots were not selected.
- The independent CLI checks reproduced the four behavior defects below. These checks gave no warning, except the machine-kind refusal in item 3.

Extra suites run:

I searched the Rust sources for the changed golden paths. These two suites read the new directories. I ran each again, in addition to the quick gate:

- `cargo test -j 16 -p camcraft-post --test waterjet_iso_post`: 7 passed.
- `cargo test -j 16 -p camcraft-post --test script_waterjet_iso`: 11 passed.

The importer rule does not apply. No importer or STEP fixture changed.

Independent mutation checks:

I ran two mutations from the PR's list. I changed one check at a time in the local review worktree.

| Mutation | Pin | Check removed | Check restored |
|---|---|---|---|
| Remove `travelOk()` | `waterjet_post_refuses_a_cut_outside_the_stated_travel` | RED, exit 101 | GREEN |
| Disable the Z-cut check | `waterjet_post_refuses_a_z_cut_and_a_cycle` | RED, exit 101 | GREEN |

Both red tests failed because the expected refusal was absent. The restored tests passed. The worktree is clean after restoration.

Requested before merge:

1. **Keep full-circle cuts when the post uses chords.** `crates/post/src/post/program_bounds.rs:101`. A valid radius-10 full-circle record starts and ends at `(10, 0)`. The circular option writes `G3 X10 Y0 I-10 J0 F300`. The linear option writes only `G1 X10 Y0 F300`, with no warning. The cut disappears. The existing `recorded/streams/full_circle_raw.cnc` uses equal endpoints. `segments3` treats equal endpoints as zero sweep. Split the circle before tessellation, or refuse it by name. Add tests for both directions.

2. **Reset the rapid cache when the work offset changes.** `assets/posts/waterjet-iso.cps:290`. I posted two sections with G54, then G55 and `OriginX=100`. The first section ends with `G0 X0 Y0`. The next section must rapid to absolute X100, which also formats as `X0 Y0` in G55. The cache removes that rapid. The output after G55 starts with the jet-on words, then `G1 X10 Y0`. It gives no warning. The jet opens at the old physical position. Clear the cache when the coordinate frame changes. Add a test with two work offsets.

3. **Carry the waterjet kind through the machine mirror.** `assets/posts/waterjet-iso.cps:148`. I supplied a valid vendor-tree machine with `general.kind: waterjet` and linear X/Y axes. The CLI parses it, then calls `machine::mirror`. The mirror drops the waterjet kind. This new check then reports `Review waterjet is not declared a waterjet machine` and writes no cut moves. Carry the kind through the mirror. Add a CLI test with a vendor-tree waterjet machine, rather than only the synthetic top-level `kind` object.

4. **Refuse a chord tolerance that the hard cap cannot meet.** `crates/post/src/post/program_bounds.rs:102`. A radius-1000 half circle with `chordTolerance=0.0001` produces 1,024 chords. I measured a maximum sagitta of `0.0011765482981900277` mm. This is more than eleven times the stated tolerance. The engine gives no warning. `segments3` silently caps the chord count. Check the required chord count or the resulting error. Meet the stated tolerance, or refuse the arc by name. Add a test that reaches the cap.

5. **Supply the required heavy-lane results.** `crates/cl/src/cl/jet.rs:18` and the PR body, Tests. The changed CL source reaches every app and motion heavy target. `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main --dry-run` selects 234 steps. The PR body names no heavy run. Current upstream rules require these results on the final head before the PR is ready. Run the reached heavy lanes after the fixes. State the head and results in the body. The dry run is not a pass.

Notes:

- The existing large files grow: `engine.rs` to 653 lines, `cnc.rs` to 1,074 lines, and `mod.rs` to 722 lines. This size note does not block the PR.
- The heavy lanes were planned but not run in this review. The PR needs changes regardless of the default-suite results.
- The isolated post inputs and NC outputs are under `/tmp`. No review evidence was committed or pushed.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Addressed:

1. Full-circle chord cuts now retain both directions. Pin: `linearize_full_circles_keeps_both_directions`.
2. Coordinate-frame changes clear the rapid cache. Pin: `waterjet_rapid_cache_resets_when_the_coordinate_frame_changes`.
3. The mirror preserves the waterjet kind. Pin: `the_cli_posts_a_vendor_tree_waterjet_machine`. This test runs the CLI with a vendor-tree machine.
4. The post refuses a tolerance that the chord cap cannot meet. Pin: `linearize_arcs_refuses_a_tolerance_below_the_chord_cap`.
5. The required heavy lanes ran on `b8e5e7ef21b9595a41614db04ddabf27efd5f68f`. The PR body records their results.

All four pins pass. Each removed fix made its pin RED with an assertion failure. Each restored fix made its pin GREEN.

Quick gate: GREEN, 997 steps, 35.4 minutes. Clippy: GREEN on all eight project crates, with `--all-targets -- -D warnings`.

Heavy gate: RED, 234 steps, one failed step, 42.0 minutes. The failed test is `the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean` in `app heavy: pocket3d_hsm`.

The original head `fe3c8f6e029a44ddae4a4c5d0f93f95d58b60d9f` has the same failure. Both heads produce `(3158, 3130, 1141)`. Linux expects `(4726, 4698, 549)`. No unrelated change was made. The PR remains a draft.

New head: `b8e5e7ef21b9595a41614db04ddabf27efd5f68f`.

Please re-review this head.

Requested before merge:

1. **Keep the Z refusal when an arc becomes chords.** `assets/posts/waterjet-iso.cps:318`, with subdivision at `crates/post/src/post/engine.rs:349`. The post checks each chord's Z change. It does not check the original arc's total Z change. A radius-1000 half circle from Z0 to Z0.1 becomes 352 chords. Each chord changes Z by less than 0.0005 mm. With `arcs=circular`, this input gives the named Z refusal. With `arcs=linear`, it gives no warning and writes 352 XY-only G1 blocks. The Z motion disappears. Validate the original arc before subdivision, or preserve its total Z change for the refusal. Add a regression for both arc modes.

   I used a vendor-tree waterjet machine with X and Y travel of `[-2000, 2000]` mm. The input was:

   ```text
   PARAM StartX 1000
   WATERJET ABRASIVE
   SECTION
   Rapid X 1000000 Y 0 Z 0
   JET ON C0 OUTER
   Arc CCW X -1000000 Y 0 Z 100 F300000 I 0 J 0
   JET OFF C0
   ENDSECTION
   ```

2. **Resolve the red required quick-gate step.** `crates/app/tests/default_machine_missing.rs:160`. The test checks that all stderr lacks `Face1`. The CLI emits an INFO generation message for `Face1`, before the correct refusal for `Setup2` and `Face2`. Thus the assertion fails. The test and its app code are unchanged from current main; I do not attribute this failure to the waterjet patch. Check the refusal diagnostic separately from the generation log, then run the required gate again. The current result is not green.

   The separate rerun gives:

   ```text
   thread 'a_missing_default_machine_file_refuses_the_post_per_operation' (495) panicked at crates/app/tests/default_machine_missing.rs:160:5:
   2026-11-21T04:00:00.695702Z  INFO generate{op=Face1}: camcraft_app::operation::generate::run_job: generated kind=Face moves=42 warnings=0 ms=1
   camcraft-cli: post: post blocked - machine of Setup2 for Face2: the default machine file 3axis-vmc.mch cannot be read (default machine: 3axis-vmc.mch in /tmp/camcraft-2319-per-op-490/assets/machines: No such file or directory (os error 2)) - mount a machine on the setup, or reinstall the file
   test result: FAILED. 8 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 0.27s
   ```

Notes:

- The diff has no UI change. No before/after screenshots are required.
- The diff adds no dependency and changes no workflow, build script, or file under `scripts/`.
- No review evidence was committed or pushed.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Addressed:

1. Chord generation retains the original arc Z change. The waterjet post gives the named refusal in both arc modes. Pin: `waterjet_post_refuses_a_helical_arc_in_both_arc_modes`.
2. The missing-machine test checks the refusal separately from INFO logs. Pin: `a_missing_default_machine_file_refuses_the_post_per_operation`.

Both pins pass. Removing each fix made its pin RED with exit 101. Restoring each fix made its pin GREEN.

New head: `ca7ba50664f6d4605b96f468b17eccc6a04f5821`.

Quick gate: GREEN, all 997 steps. Clippy: GREEN on all eight project crates, with `--all-targets -- -D warnings`.

Heavy gate: RED, 234 steps, one failed step. The failed test is `the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean` in `app heavy: pocket3d_hsm`. The prior head `b8e5e7ef21b9595a41614db04ddabf27efd5f68f` gives the same failure and counts `(3158, 3130, 1141)`. All other reached heavy steps pass. No unrelated fix was made.

The PR body records the results. The PR remains a draft. Please re-review this head.

Independent mutations:

Requested before merge:

1. **Refuse a section with no waterjet header before dropping its motion.** `assets/posts/waterjet-iso.cps:320`.
   After `ENDSECTION`, the engine clears the header from its base properties.
   The next `onSection` sees stale script properties and opens the preamble.
   The next feed then reaches `cutOk` with no header. `jetOk()` returns false without a warning.
   With a valid vendor-tree waterjet machine, this independent input exits successfully with no warning:

   ```text
   WATERJET
   SECTION
   Rapid X 0 Y 0 Z 0
   JET ON C0 OUTER
   Feed X 1000 Y 0 Z 0 F300000
   JET OFF C0
   ENDSECTION
   SECTION
   Feed X 10000 Y 0 Z 0 F300000
   ENDSECTION
   ```
